newsitem.title: USA: McDonnell Douglas net rises 1.6 percent.
newsitem.headline: McDonnell Douglas net rises 1.6 percent.

text.p: McDonnell Douglas Corp. Thursday said earnings rose 1.6 percent in the third quarter, about in line with expectations on Wall Street, led by strength in its military and commercial aircraft businesses.

The company, a major defence contractor as well as a manufacturer of commercial jetliners, said earnings rose to $195 million, or 90 cents a share, in the quarter, from $192 million, or 85 cents a share, in the 1995 quarter.
Sales edged lower to $3.31 billion from $3.35 billion.
The results were a penny shy of analysts' forecasts of 91 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks estimates.
Results for the latest quarter included a previously announced charge of $9 million, or 4 cents a share, for settlement of claims stemming from a 1984 contract for T-45 trainer jets for the Navy.
The year-ago period included earnings of $25 million, or 11 cents a share, from resolution of tax issues.

The St. Louis-based company said that the the 99-day strike at its St. Louis plant was not expected to significantly hurt results. The strike ended in mid-September after 6,400 machinists ratified a new contract.
Operating earnings in the military aircraft segment rose nearly 7 percent, led by strength in its C-17 military transport and Apache helicopter business, McDonnell Douglas said.

The commercial aircraft business had operating earnings of $23 million in the latest quarter, compared with a loss of $7 million in the 1995 quarter. The parts and service business bolstered results, partly offset by losses incurred on the company's MD-95 jetliner programme, currently in development.
Earnings in missiles, space and electronic systems fell 17 percent.
Net earnings for the first nine months of 1996 were $581 million, a record, up from $520 million in the 1995 period, the company said. Sales fell 9 percent to $9.74 billion from $10.60 billion.
